title: The diffusive spectral gap of the qubit eSWAP chain
abstract: We prove that the second-moment Hamiltonian of the open qubit eSWAP chain has a diffusive spectral gap, resolving a conjecture of Li, Zheng, Liu, Jiang, and Liu. We also characterise the ground space on every connected interaction graph with at least five vertices and prove a uniform lower bound for the unnormalised complete-graph gap. We apply these results to sequential and brickwork circuits and prove that the periodic chain also has a diffusive spectral gap.
summary: This paper rigorously proves that the spectral gap of the open qubit eSWAP chain scales diffusively as $n^{-2}$, resolving an open conjecture. It characterizes the ground state space for general connected interaction graphs and applies these findings to analyze the convergence properties of quantum circuits. This is crucial for understanding the mixing time and efficiency of quantum information processing protocols.
main_problem: The paper proves that the second-moment Hamiltonian of the open qubit eSWAP chain possesses a diffusive spectral gap, resolving a prior conjecture.
main_result: The spectral gap $\Delta(H_n)$ for the open qubit eSWAP chain scales as $\Theta(n^{-2})$, and the ground space $	ext{Ker } H_G$ is characterized as the sum of direct and crossed pairing spaces for $n \ge 5$.
method: The analysis combines spectral gap estimates, utilizing techniques like Aldous' spectral-gap theorem and solving Poisson equations, alongside decomposing the Hamiltonian into interchange and reaction projections.
model_or_system: The system models an open qubit eSWAP chain on a graph $G$, governed by a Hamiltonian $H_G$ constructed from local second-moment twirl operators ($T^{(2)}$) and projections ($p_e, q_e$).
key_observables: Spectral Gap ($\Delta(H_n)$), Ground Space ($	ext{Ker } H_G$), and the scaling behavior of these quantities.
important_parameters: The number of qubits $n$, and the structure of the interaction graph $G$ (e.g., path, complete graph $K_n$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the local interchange-reaction decomposition ($h_e = p_e + q_e$) and specific graph structures for the theorems presented.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by establishing the spectral gap conjecture for the eSWAP-chain Hamiltonian, characterizing the ground space for general connected graphs, and providing bounds for the complete graph case.
why_interesting: The work provides rigorous spectral bounds for quantum circuits based on local interactions (eSWAP), which directly impacts the understanding of mixing times and quantum gate fidelity in quantum computation.
